manual_review_reason: Radio One publicly designates music@r1.co.nz for music submissions and also lists a physical delivery address. Its linked alternative-radio servicing guide asks for a personal email, contact details, a correctly named and tagged download at minimum 320 kbps MP3 quality, focus songs and a one-page information sheet. The guide is written around New Zealand artists, so a human must confirm whether the specific MarcsMusic release is eligible and relevant as an international submission, select the correct track and specialty-program fit, verify the current delivery preference, release timing, explicit-content policy, rights and AI-origin requirements, and approve the final message before any email or parcel is sent.

Radio Control publicly lists music@radiocontrol.org.nz for Music Submissions and a station postal address, but the official contact page does not state the accepted audio format, attachment or download-link rules, release-age limits, explicit-content requirements, rights declarations, AI-origin policy or response expectations. A human must confirm the live submission requirements, choose a suitable alternative/electronic track, avoid large unsolicited attachments, approve the pitch and decide between email and optional physical delivery before contacting the station.

95bFM exposes a first-party Submit Music link in its official site navigation, but the linked page could not be passively rendered during verification, so its current fields, accepted file or link formats, locality rules, consent language, CAPTCHA or anti-spam controls, login requirements and any optional commercial choices remain unverified. The site's public email link is Cloudflare-protected and was not decoded. A human must open the official page normally, review all live requirements and security controls, confirm MarcsMusic eligibility and track fit, and complete any submission without automation or bypassing protection.
